---
title: "The Code Page"
subtitle: "Continuously updated codes discussed in lectures"
---

As a registered PHYD57 student, you are free to copy and develop the programs below to do more things, change their output style, etc. **Knowledge of basic structures and methods used in these codes is a course requirement.**

## 🐍 Python Refresher & Introductory Methods
- `simple_vectors-03.py`: Compares Python loops vs NumPy array operations.
- `simple_IO.py` / `simple_stat.py`: Basic I/O and statistics in Python.
- `plot_exp_approx-1.py` / `plot_cos_approx-1.py`: Taylor series expansion and plotting with Matplotlib.
- `simple_mtc_pi.py`: Calculation of Pi by Monte Carlo.
- `simple_bisec.py` / `simple_newton.py`: Bisection and Newton's methods for root finding.

## 🚀 High Performance Computing (HPC) & C/Fortran
- `laplacian-5t.py`: Image processing using the heat/diffusion Laplace operator stencil (NumPy).
- `ifor-laplace3-dp.f90` / `pgf-laplace3-dp.f95`: Laplace stencil in Fortran (CPU vs GPU compilation).
- `711-brute.py` / `711-brute.c` / `711-brute.f95`: Cracking the 711 puzzle using brute force across Python, C, and Fortran.
- `simpler-nb-1.f90`: Loop over a 2D array in Fortran demonstrating throughput and RAM bandwidth limits.

## 🔄 Calling C from Python
- `libfunc.c` & `use_libc.c`: Building and linking a shared C library.
- `fun_lib0.c` & `callingC-0-py2.py`: Calling a compiled C library from Python via `ctypes`.

## 🎨 Graphics in Fortran/C (DISLIN)
- `volcano-disl.f90`: F90 code generating DISLIN graphics directly from Fortran. Showcases OpenMP parallelization scheduling and critical sections.

## ⚡ CUDA C and CUDA Fortran
- `simple_saxpy_cuda.cu`: SAXPY (Single-Precision A*X Plus Y) in CUDA C.
- `cuda-perf.f95`: Fortran 95 version with CUDA diagnostics showing bandwidth and compute performance.
- `tetraDg-3.f95`: GPU version of the tetrahedra problem using CUDA Fortran.

## 🧠 Machine Learning & Neural Networks
- `inv-pend-ctrl-3orig+plt.f95`: Sequential Fortran code solving the inverted broomstick problem using a simple Neural Network (3 hidden neurons, 1 output).
